text:
maria: FYI - BigCorp legal just told their compliance team we need a pinned model for their EU workloads by EOW. They require deterministic outputs for specific prompts and an auditable benchmark.
ajay: Oof. Is this a hard constraint from contract or a one-off ask?
maria: Contract clause. They can withhold payments if we don't provide a stable, pinned artifact for their account.
kim: Ok. Two paths: 1) Pin an existing stable weight (v2.1) + provide eval report, or 2) Offer a compatibility shim (deterministic post-processing) that sits on top of our usual variants. 
leo: Given timeline (5 working days) we should avoid new training/finetune. Option 1 plausible if v2.1 passes a lightweight determinism bench.
sarah: What does the compliance bench need? seed fixation? token-level diffs?
maria: They listed: deterministic outputs for 20 canonical prompts, reproducible inference with same model binary + config, and latency p95 < 200ms for their traffic profile. Also want an artifacts list: model hash, quantization step, and exact server config.
rachel: We need to align with eng-runtime on whether a quantized build still meets determinism. Quantization can introduce non-determinism unless we fix kernels.
ajay: Proposal: create a "lite audit" benchmark: 20 canonical prompts + 100 random prompts drawn from customer logs (anonymized). Run on candidate v2.1 cpu/gpu/quantized variants. Measure: token-by-token equality for canonical prompts, embedding cosine stability, latency p50/p95, and cost delta.
kim: +1. Add an acceptance rule: canonical prompts must be exact-match or differ only in whitespace/punctation normalization (we'll define normalization). For random prompts, allow small top-k/token deviations but track KL/ROUGE metrics.
leo: How much eng capacity do we need? I can free up a 4-GPU canary pool for 24h if we commit to automation.
sarah: I can assemble the 20 canonical prompts and a normalization script. Suggest we use this repo path: https://git.redwood/company/audit-bench (private).
maria: Great. I'll tell BigCorp we have a plan and aim to deliver audit artifacts + pinned model by Friday EOD.
rachel: Ops question: do we expose a pinned model endpoint per-tenant? Because BigCorp wants a dedicated URL for audit.
ajay: Short-term: we can create a tenant-scoped route that maps to the pinned model variant and returns model_hash header. Longer term, we should support per-tenant pinned configs in catalog.
kim: Quick config snippet for canary manifest (will hand off to eng):
```
route: /v1/generate?tenant=bigcorp
model: redwood/v2.1-2025-03-01
pin: true
hash-header: X-Model-Hash
canary: 4xA10G
```
leo: deploy-bot: Canary started for model=redwood/v2.1-2025-03-01 on pool=canary-4g. (automated note) :rocket:
maria: Two negotiation points with BigCorp: 1) Are they willing to accept quantized model if we provide exact audit artifacts? 2) If latency SLO can't be met on their traffic in EU, can we negotiate extended SLA credits? I'll draft options.
sarah: Also note downstream customers using same tenant should be notified; ops must ensure traffic shaping to avoid noisy neighbors during canary.
rachel: I'll add audit logging + KMS fingerprint to the manifest. Need legal to sign off on artifacts list; looping in @legal later.
ajay: Next steps: (1) kim + leo run lite bench on v2.1 (24h), (2) sarah collates canonical prompts (today), (3) maria preps comms for BigCorp (today), (4) rachel and ops enable tenant route and hash header (tomorrow).
maria: Thanks. If we hit any blocker, drop updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
